queue.title: F272 -- settle whether the lost terminal status row is the harness or the product
queue.detail: Found iteration 7 by the Hub suite, filed in scripts/drive/FINDINGS.md as F272 (B). record_agent_output (output_recording.py:92-94) does db.add -> commit -> db.refresh(row), and the refresh's primary-key SELECT finds NO ROW: sqlalchemy InvalidRequestError 'Could not refresh instance'. It escapes into _execute_run's catch-all (agent_trigger.py:2215), becomes a log line, and the run ends with NO terminal status row -- the exact thing phase 2 exists to guarantee, and the F190 shape again. MEASURED: 2 failures in 20 runs of test_a_stopped_run_persists_its_terminal_status_line ALONE (~10%), 1 in 6 of the whole file; NOT cross-test interference. Introduced by phase 2 (commit 3b1b8f0) -- before it the finalize block was a bare broadcast with no DB write. STEP 1: re-run that test against a FILE-BACKED sqlite URL with a normal pool instead of sqlite+aiosqlite:///:memory: (conftest.py:19; db/engine.py:34-38 sets no poolclass, so the in-memory dialect shares ONE DBAPI connection across every concurrent session and can interleave COMMIT/ROLLBACK). If it stops failing the mechanism is the harness and the fix is there; if it still fails it is a product race on the STOP path -- the one path where a request handler's session runs concurrently with the run's own -- and F272 becomes severity A and phase-2 work. DO NOT 'fix' it by deleting db.refresh(row): the refresh is the messenger, the row really is absent, and removing the read converts a logged failure into a silent one (only row.timestamp needs it, for the broadcast payload). Capture pytest output to a FILE with --tb=long -- two earlier sightings tonight lost their traceback to a `| tail`. Separately worth recording either way: _execute_run's catch-all swallowing a failed TERMINAL-STATUS write is its own weakness.
